Veterinary Practice Bill at Second Reading, creating a Veterinary Council to register and discipline vets

Second Reading8 April 2026 bill-792

A Bill at Second Reading, moved by the Minister of State for National Development on behalf of the Minister for National Development, that establishes a Veterinary Council to register veterinarians and regulate the practice of veterinary medicine in Singapore.

The Minister said vets will have to be registered with the new Council and hold a valid practising certificate to practise, and that the Registrar must publish registered vets' particulars so the public can search for and verify a vet's registration status and place of practice. The maximum financial penalty for unlawful practice or misrepresentation as a vet rises from $10,000 to $50,000. Existing AVS-licensed vets will be temporarily deemed duly qualified and must obtain registration and a practising certificate within a stipulated grace period to continue practising.

Open questions from this debate (10)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • Whether a locally offered veterinary degree programme will be introduced, and on what timeline.
  • Whether regulation will be extended to pet groomers and dog trainers, and when.
  • What the prescribed conditions and supervision arrangements for non-vets, including community caregivers, will say in practice.
  • Whether a transition period will apply to enforcement against community animal caregivers performing basic first aid.
  • Whether the exemption power under clause 86 will be used to carve out community animal welfare activities.
  • Whether fee benchmarks, itemised billing or mandatory fee disclosures will be introduced, and when.
  • What the registration and practising certificate fees will be.
  • How many investigators will be appointed and whether a dedicated enforcement unit will be set up.
  • Whether Industry Abuse Protections will be extended to veterinarians.
  • Whether an ITE pathway into veterinary or animal care work will be developed.

Sir, the Veterinary Practice Bill establishes a new professional regulatory body, the Veterinary Council, to register veterinarians, or vets, and to regulate the practice of veterinary medicine in Singapore. Today, vets in Singapore are licensed under the Animals and Birds Act (ABA). This framework has served us well in safeguarding animal health and welfare, and in protecting human health from animal diseases. However, our vet sector has evolved and matured significantly. I support the direction of the Bill. At the same time, I would like to raise one central concern on behalf of many pet owners, which is: how do we strengthen professionalism in the sector while ensuring that vet care remains affordable and accessible? How this page was made

Built from the official Hansard record (Parliament of Singapore Official Reports). No news reporting was used. Briefs are written by software from the transcript and every key point carries the verbatim words it was drawn from.
